## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vevacanahāravibhaṅga* ("Conveying Synonyms: Analysis") is the thirteenth section of the *Netti* (*Nettippakaraṇa*), preserved in the late canonical and post-canonical strata of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The methodological category upon which the analysis is based is listed in modern surveys of Pali literature under the heading *Vevacanahāra* [Norman 1983]. One modern translation of the text into English is cataloged on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

Curated passage-level parallels identified by SuttaCentral connect the *Vevacanahāravibhaṅga* to the *Peṭakopadesa* (specifically Pe 1, *Ariyasaccappakāsanapaṭhamabhūmi*) as well as to an earlier analytical section of the *Netti* itself, the *Yuttihāravibhaṅga* (Ne 6) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral also notes ties to specific canonical discourses, including the *Paṭhamamahānāmasutta* (AN 11.11), the *Mahānāmasutta* (AN 6.10), and the *Parāyanasutta* (SN 43.44) [SuttaCentral].

Automated analysis by DharmaNexus registers extensive Pali-internal text reuse, recording 351 matching passages shared across 44 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. In alignment with SuttaCentral's canonical references, the largest sutta reuse partners occur in the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 3, AN 4, AN 5, AN 6, AN 8, AN 11), the *Saṁyutta Nikāya* (SN 40, SN 55), and the *Majjhima Nikāya* (MN 137) [DharmaNexus]. Major non-sutta parallels and reuses include the *Vibhaṅga* (Vb 18, *Dhammahadayavibhaṅga*), the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 1.1, *Ñāṇakathā*), and the *Visuddhimagga*, in addition to comprehensive treatment in its commentary (*Nettippakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā*) and sub-commentary (*Nettivibhāvinī*) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records cross-language machine alignments with the Sanskrit *Pañcakrama* and a Tibetan treatise (D2565) [DharmaNexus].
